title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the preceding pages). Start from an extension of discrete groups (27): 1 → M → G → H → 1, with M a free Z-module of finite type and H acting on M by conjugation. Over the base S_0 (apparently Spec Z) Grothendieck builds a group scheme extension (38): 1 → M̲ → G̲ → H_{S_0} → 1.
- Here M̲ is the vector group attached to M, with M̲(A) = M⊗_Z A.
- G̲ is the pushout of the constant group scheme G_{S_0} along M_{S_0} → M̲. The H-action on M̲ comes from the action on M.
- Taking points over an affine S = Spec A gives (39): 1 → M⊗A → G̲(A) → H → 1, receiving a map from (27).

Top of this page: functoriality. A morphism of extensions (40), (M,G,H) → (M',G',H'), induces a commutative cube (41). Its four rows are:
- the constant extension M_{S_0} → G_{S_0} → H_{S_0};
- its primed analogue M'_{S_0} → G'_{S_0} → H'_{S_0};
- the 'algebraized' extension M̲ → G̲ → H_{S_0};
- the primed algebraized extension M̲' → G̲' → H'_{S_0}.
The arrows are the canonical maps from constant to algebraized objects and the maps induced by (40).

Section 4. The margin title is hard to read; it plausibly reads 'Exemple: schématisation (?) des groupes discrets résolubles'.
- The model case: a lattice M with a finite-index sublattice M_i gives 1 → M_i → M → M/M_i → 1. This is a special case of (27) with G = M and H = M/M_i finite.
- General case: start from (27) and take M_i ⊂ M of finite index and normal in G. Since M is abelian, normal in G is the same as H-stable. This gives (43): 1 → M_i → G → H_i := G/M_i → 1.
- H_i is itself the extension (44): 1 → M/M_i → H_i → H → 1, the pushout of (27) along M → M/M_i.

Where this goes (next page).
- Such H-stable M_i are cofinal among all finite-index subgroups (indeed nM ⊂ M_i is characteristic).
- To each one applies the construction, giving group scheme extensions 1 → M̲_i → E_i → H_{i,S_0} → 1.
- As i varies these form a projective system, i.e. a pro-group scheme over Z. Grothendieck checks the transition maps are affine, reducing to the map E(M_i,M_j) → E(M_i,M_i) = M̲_i, where E(M_i,M_j) is the extension of (M_i/M_j)_{S_0} by M̲_j.

The aim seems to be a pro-group-scheme 'arithmetic schematization' over Z of a discrete virtually-abelian (and, by iteration, solvable/polycyclic) group. It mixes the profinite information (finite quotients H_i) with the algebraic information (vector-group parts M̲_i, which become isomorphic over Q). This sits in the continuation of La Longue Marche, i.e. the discrete-versus-profinite study of fundamental groups.
errors: Equation numbering is duplicated: the cube diagram is numbered (41), the sequence 1→M_i→M→M/M_i→1 is also labelled (41) in the image (should be (42)), and the next page reuses (41) again.

No mathematical error on this page. On the next page Grothendieck's crossed-out restriction to H finite is indeed unnecessary for cofinality, since nM ⊂ M_i is characteristic in M and hence stable under any H.

ideas.what: Functorial algebraization of an extension 1→M→G→H→1 (M a lattice) into a group scheme extension of the constant group H_{S_0} by the vector group M⊗G_a, via pushout of constant group schemes.
ideas.modern_name: Algebraic hull / pushout to an affine (vector) group extension; arithmetic version of Malcev/Mostow algebraic hulls
ideas.usually_credited_to: Malcev (nilpotent, 1949); Mostow and Hochschild (algebraic hulls of polycyclic groups, 1960s-70s)

ideas.what: Functoriality cube (41) relating constant and algebraized extensions under a morphism of extensions.

Using the H-stable finite-index sublattices M_i to build a projective system of group scheme extensions E_i over Z, i.e. a pro-group scheme 'schematization' of a discrete solvable group combining finite quotients with vector-group parts.
ideas.modern_name: Schematization of discrete groups over Z / pro-algebraic (affine) completion over Z; related to Toën's 'schématisation' and affine stacks
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck's schematization problem (Pursuing Stacks era) as developed by Toën (2000s); pro-algebraic completions by Hochschild-Mostow and others
ideas.where_published: The general schematization idea is mentioned in Pursuing Stacks / letters; this explicit construction for solvable discrete groups is not known to me in published form

ideas.what: Pushout along M→M/M_i gives the finite-type quotient H_i = G/M_i as an extension of H by M/M_i (44).

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches, in the La Longue Marche continuation, an explicit arithmetic (over Spec Z) schematization of discrete virtually-abelian/solvable groups. The ingredients are pro-systems of group scheme extensions of finite constant groups by vector groups M_i⊗G_a, indexed by finite-index invariant sublattices. This is a concrete integral model differing from the usual pro-unipotent/pro-algebraic completions over a field and from the profinite completion.
missed.quote: Exemple [schématisation?] des groupes discrets résolubles ... pour tout sous-groupe M_i d'indice fini dans M, distingué dans G i.e. stable par H, on a une suite exacte 1 → M_i → G → G/M_i → 1
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral/arithmetic schematization of homotopy types and fundamental groups (Toën, and later work on integral affine stacks and pro-algebraic completions over Z) is an active theme. An explicit early Grothendieck model for solvable groups, tied to the discrete-vs-profinite questions of anabelian geometry, may be of historical and possibly technical interest. Its content as given here is a fairly elementary construction, however.

deep.surprise_reason: The page itself is a routine functoriality diagram plus the setup of finite-index sublattices. Its interest lies in context: an apparently unpublished attempt at an integral pro-group-scheme schematization of discrete solvable groups within the La Longue Marche continuation. That fits known Grothendieck themes (schematization), so it is not shocking.
transcription_corrections: Groups G, G', G̲, G̲' are written as fraktur 𝔊 in the image.

Cube diagram rows: 1→M_{S_0}→𝔊_{S_0}→H_{S_0}→1; 1→M'_{S_0}→𝔊'_{S_0}→H'_{S_0}→1; 1→M̲→𝔊̲→H_{S_0}→1; 1→M̲'→𝔊̲'→H'→1 (the last H' appears underlined but is the constant group H'_{S_0}). There are diagonal arrows between unprimed and primed objects and vertical arrows from constant to underlined rows, with equality on the H_{S_0} column.
The sequence 1→M_i→M→M/M_i→1 is labelled '(41)' in the image, not '(42)'.
Margin title is hard to read; it plausibly reads 'Exemple: schématisation des groupes discrets résolubles' rather than 'ℕ-adinisation discrète'.
Line after (43) reads 'et maintenant H_i = G/M_i' with an arrow noting H_i; the next line reads 'est extension de' (with a struck-out word).
